The Mere

Below the still water the drowned village keeps its lights — a window here, a hearth there, burning on under the mere the way a thing remembered goes on being lit. On the stillest nights the church bell rings for its people yet.

WINIFRED MARLOWE
the miller's daughter · who numbered the stones
and carried Hollowmere uphill

The water keeps every light, and the house keeps her name. · back to the study
